newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Democracy advocates have accused the government of packing the Constitution Drafting Assembly with its supporters and compromising the drive for political reform. The reaction came after Parliament announced formally the 99 constitution writers elected in a process in which most of the government favourites prevailed. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Deputy Police Director General Salang Bunnag has proposed arming security guards at commercial banks and jewellery shops, due to the recent series of armed robberies. He says he has also asked the Bank of Thailand to seek cooperation from commercial banks to install closed-circuit television as part of security measures. (THE NATION)

- The government needs effective measures to deport illegal immigrants who failed to register with the Labour Ministry as their presence affects national security, says a director of the Thai Development Research Institute. The director refers to a programme which allows existing illegal workers from Cambodia, Laos and Burma to register with the Ministry and continue working in 43 of the country's provinces for two years. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand's (BOT) economic growth projection for 1997 stands at 7.1 percent over 1996, which reflects the optimism of the Commerce Ministry's prediction. The central bank's primary economic figures in 1996 shows the year's economic growth standing at 6.7 percent against 8.7 percent a year ago, as a result of the economic slowdown and a significant decline in exports. (BUSINES DAY)

- Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee has promised he will decide within the first quarter of next year how many new insurance licences will be issued by the government. He declined to commit himself to exact numbers, saying only that he would review the criteria by considering market supply and demand. (THE NATION)

- Serviced apartment developer President Park Properties Plc has formed a joint venture with regional property fund South East Asia Property Co to build and manage serviced apartments in Asia. The new company will provide property management services for 884 existing serviced apartments and the new residential development. (THE NATION)
